title: Siddu
jainNotes: Contains ginger in the stuffing. For Jain version, omit ginger and use only green chilli.

ingredients.name: Walnuts / poppy seeds / lentil paste for stuffing

recipe: Knead wheat flour with yeast, a little sugar, salt and warm water into a soft dough. Ferment 1–2 hours.
Prepare stuffing by grinding roasted walnuts/poppy seeds or boiled lentils with ginger, green chilli, coriander and salt.
Divide dough, stuff with filling, shape into oval or half-moon buns and steam for 15–20 minutes till cooked.
Serve hot with a generous amount of desi ghee and chutney.
tips: Iconic steamed bread of Kullu, Mandi, Shimla regions – energy-dense and perfect for cold weather.
Traditionally carried by shepherds; modern fillings include potato or paneer.

title: Babru
jainNotes: Contains asafoetida. Standard hing may contain wheat/gum. Use Jain-certified hing to make it Jain-friendly.
recipe: Grind soaked urad dal with spices into a thick paste for stuffing.
Knead flour into a soft dough. Divide, stuff with urad paste, seal and roll into thick puris.
Deep-fry in medium-hot oil till golden and puffed.
Serve hot with curd, chutney or tea.
tips: Popular in Mandi, Kangra and Chamba – similar to a stuffed bhatura or kachori.
Savoury version is most common; sweet jaggery versions also exist.

title: Aktori
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible. Ensure buckwheat flour is pure and not contaminated with other flours.

ingredients.name: Milk or water, sugar or jaggery

recipe: Mix buckwheat and wheat flour with milk/water and a little sugar/jaggery into a pouring batter.
Heat a tawa or pan, pour batter like a thick pancake and cook on both sides with ghee till golden.
Serve hot with ghee, honey or stewed apples.
tips: Traditional Lahaul-Spiti / high-altitude pancake, often festive.
Buckwheat gives a distinctive nutty flavour and is well-suited to cold climates.

title: Chana Madra
jainNotes: Contains onion and ginger-garlic in traditional preparation - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Ghee, cumin, cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaf
Turmeric, coriander powder, red chilli, garam masala, salt

recipe: Pressure-cook soaked chickpeas till soft.
Whisk yogurt till smooth. Heat ghee, add whole spices, then the yogurt carefully on low heat, stirring continuously to avoid curdling. Cook till it thickens and oil separates.
Add the chickpeas, remaining spices and salt. Simmer gently till the gravy coats the chana.
Serve with rice as part of a Himachali dham.
tips: Signature yogurt-based curry of Himachali dham feasts.
Slow cooking and continuous stirring of yogurt are essential.

title: Sepu Badi
jainNotes: Contains onion, ginger, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Urad dal or mixed dal badi (sun-dried dumplings)

recipe: Soak and lightly fry the dried badi. Blanch and puree spinach if using.
Temper whole spices, sauté onion, ginger-garlic and tomato. Add yogurt and spice powders; cook till oil separates.
Add spinach puree and the badi. Simmer till the gravy thickens and badi absorb the flavours.
Serve with rice or roti as part of dham.
tips: Specialty of Mandi region – protein-rich lentil dumplings in a green gravy.
Often prepared for weddings and festive dhams.

title: Tudkiya Bhath
jainNotes: Contains onion, potato and root vegetables - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Whole spices (cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaf), cumin, garam masala

recipe: Heat ghee, temper whole spices and cumin. Add vegetables if using and sauté.
Add washed rice and dal, spices and salt. Sauté briefly.
Add water (about 3 cups) and cook covered or pressure-cook till rice and dal are soft and flavours meld.
Serve hot as a one-pot meal or with madra and kadhi.
tips: Fragrant spiced rice-lentil dish common in Himachali dhams.
Slightly richer and more aromatic than everyday khichdi.

title: Chha Gosht
jainNotes: Contains meat - not consumed by Jains who follow strict vegetarianism.

ingredients.name: Whole spices, coriander powder, red chilli, garam masala

recipe: Marinate mutton with yogurt, ginger-garlic and salt for at least 1 hour.
Heat ghee/oil, brown onions and whole spices. Add the marinated mutton and sear well.
Add remaining spices and a little water. Slow-cook or pressure-cook till meat is tender and the gravy is thick and tangy from the yogurt.
Serve with rice or local bread.
tips: Yogurt-based mutton curry popular in many Himachali households.
The 'chha' refers to the buttermilk/yogurt base that tenderises the meat.

title: Rajma Madra
jainNotes: Contains onion and ginger-garlic in traditional preparation - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Ghee, whole spices (cloves, cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaf)
Coriander powder, red chilli, turmeric, garam masala, salt

recipe: Pressure-cook soaked rajma till soft.
Whisk yogurt. Heat ghee, add whole spices, then carefully add yogurt on low heat, stirring continuously till it thickens and oil separates.
Add cooked rajma, spice powders and salt. Simmer till the gravy is rich and coats the beans.
Serve with rice as part of a traditional dham.
tips: Another classic madra variation – richer and heartier than chana madra.
Essential in many regional dham menus (especially Chamba style).

title: Patande
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible. Ensure no eggs used (recipe uses milk/water).
recipe: Make a smooth pouring batter of flour and milk/water (sweeten if desired).
Pour thin circles on a hot greased tawa like a crepe or pancake. Cook on both sides till golden.
Serve hot with honey, stewed apples or ghee.
tips: Kinnauri / high-hill pancake, light and comforting.
Often paired with local fruit preserves.

title: Mittha (Sweet Rice)
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible. Ensure ghee and dry fruits are from pure sources.
recipe: Cook rice till soft. In another pan heat ghee, fry nuts and raisins.
Add the cooked rice, sugar/jaggery, cardamom and a little water or milk. Cook till the sugar dissolves and the mixture is glossy.
Serve warm as a festive sweet or dessert course of dham.
tips: Traditional sweet rice preparation served at the end of Himachali dhams.
Rich with dry fruits and ghee.

title: Khatta (Tangy Tamarind Curry)
jainNotes: Standard hing may contain wheat/gum. Use Jain-certified hing to make it Jain-friendly. Also contains optional potatoes (root vegetable).

ingredients.name: Chickpea flour or boiled potatoes / black chickpeas (optional)
Mustard, cumin, dry red chilli, curry leaves, asafoetida

recipe: Extract tamarind water. Mix with jaggery, salt and turmeric. Cook till it thickens slightly.
Temper mustard, cumin, dry red chilli and hing. Pour over the khatta.
Add boiled potatoes or black chickpeas if using and simmer briefly.
Serve as a tangy side with rice in a dham.
tips: The sweet-sour element that balances the richer madra and dal courses.
Often made with locally available souring agents.

title: Bhaturu
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible. Ensure yeast/fermented starter does not contain non-Jain additives.

ingredients.name: Oil or ghee for frying or cooking

recipe: Knead flour with fermented starter/yeast, salt and water into a soft dough. Ferment several hours or overnight.
Divide and roll into thick discs. Shallow-fry or cook on a tawa till golden and cooked through.
Serve with dal, madra or any local curry.
tips: Traditional fermented bread of rural Himachal – a daily staple in many households.
The natural fermentation gives a mild sour flavour.
